import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionsToDivisors
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafClass

/-!
# Sections to divisors — the LocalEquations construction and the class law (DAT-A)

Worksheet §2.2 step 2, made literal (`informal/spec-dat-a.md` §3): a global section of
the DAT-1 glued sheaf **is** a matching family `(s_j)` with `s_i = g_{ij}·s_j`, so once
its components are germ-regular (DAT-A2, `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionsToDivisors`)
it is a `Scheme.LocalEquations` datum on the nose. The (1e) class law
(`Cohomology/GluedSheafClass.lean`, landed while this brick was in flight) is consumed
directly — the spec's `cocycleClassOn` seam is CLOSED, no interim class carrier exists:

* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionLocalEquations` — the LocalEquations datum of a
  germ-regular global section on **any** pointed cover subordinated to the pieces
  (the (1e) subordination interface `𝒲, σ, hσ`): equations the restricted components
  `D.component s (σ y)`, ratio witnesses the subordinated transition units
  `gluedSubordUnit`;
* `sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit` — the ratio units are **exactly** the (restricted)
  transition units of the cocycle (`ratioUnit_unique`); on the piece cover the
  restriction is along `≤`-reflexivity, i.e. the units themselves;
* `sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle` — the units cocycle of the constructed datum is
  the (1e) subordinated cocycle `gluedSubordCocycle`;
* **the class law** `sectionLocalEquations_picClass`:
  `(D.sectionLocalEquations …).picClass = D.cechPicClass` — the divisor datum cut out
  by a germ-regular section presents THE class of the datum's cocycle (the Abel
  correspondence), through the landed `cechPicClass_eq_mk`. Naturality under
  refinement/subordination-choice is the landed `gluedSubordCocycle_class_eq`; unit
  rescalings and cover refinements of the constructed datum keep the class by the
  landed `LocalEquations.picClass_rescale`/`picClass_restrict`;
* `sectionLocalEquations_picClass_congr` — any two germ-regular sections on any two
  subordinated covers cut divisors of the same class;
* `sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular` — the A2-bundled wrapper on the canonical
  pointed cover (`D.pointedCover`): a fibrewise-regular global section yields the
  divisor datum outright, with class `D.cechPicClass` (`[IsNoetherianRing B]`).
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]

/-- The value of a restricted unit section is the restriction of its value. -/
private lemma val_unitsRestrict {X : Scheme.{u}} {W U : X.Opens} (h : W ≤ U)
    (u : Γ(X, U)ˣ) :
    ((X.unitsRestrict h u : Γ(X, W)ˣ) : Γ(X, W)) = X.resHom h (u : Γ(X, U)) :=
  rfl

section AffineHom

variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
variable (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
variable (𝒲 : (relCurve C B).PointedCover) (σ : relCurve C B → D.index)
variable (hσ : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ y))

/-- The defining ratio equation of the section's restricted components on the overlaps
of a subordinated pointed cover: the matching relation of the glued family, restricted
from `⊤ ⊓ Uᵢ ⊓ Uⱼ`. -/
private lemma component_ratio_eq (y y' : relCurve C B) :
    ((relCurve C B).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
        𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y' ≤ 𝒲.opens y)).op).hom
        ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)))
      = (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :
            Γ(relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'))
        * ((relCurve C B).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
            𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y' ≤ 𝒲.opens y')).op).hom
            ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y') (D.component s (σ y'))) := by
  have hle : 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'
      ≤ ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces (σ y) ⊓ D.pieces (σ y') :=
    le_inf (le_inf le_top (inf_le_left.trans (hσ y))) (inf_le_right.trans (hσ y'))
  have key := congrArg ((relCurve C B).resHom hle) (s.property (σ y) (σ y'))
  rw [map_mul] at key
  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key
  change (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_left
      ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)))
    = (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :
        Γ(relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'))
      * (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_right
          ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y') (D.component s (σ y')))
  rw [gluedSubordUnit, val_unitsRestrict, component, component]
  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom]
  exact key

/-- **Sections ↦ divisor families** (DAT-A, worksheet §2.2 step 2): a germ-regular
global section of the DAT-1 glued sheaf is a `Scheme.LocalEquations` datum on any
pointed cover subordinated to the pieces — the equations are the (restricted)
components, the ratio witnesses the subordinated transition units. Germ-regularity
(`hreg`) is DAT-A2's output (`germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors` relatively;
`Scheme.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero` on an integral field-level curve). -/
noncomputable def sectionLocalEquations
    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y)) :
    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations where
  cover := 𝒲
  eqn y := (relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y))
  regular y z hz := by
    rw [Scheme.resHom, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    exact hreg (σ y) z (hσ y hz)
  ratio_isUnit y y' :=
    ⟨gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y', D.component_ratio_eq s 𝒲 σ hσ y y'⟩

variable (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
  ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
    ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y))

@[simp]
lemma sectionLocalEquations_cover :
    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).cover = 𝒲 :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma sectionLocalEquations_eqn (y : relCurve C B) :
    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).eqn y
      = (relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)) :=
  rfl

/-- **The ratio units are exactly the cocycle's transition units** (worksheet §2.2 step
2's "ratio units EXACTLY the cocycle"), in subordinated form: by uniqueness of ratio
witnesses against a regular equation. On the piece cover the subordination is
`≤`-reflexivity and `gluedSubordUnit` is the transition unit restricted along it. -/
lemma sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit (y y' : relCurve C B) :
    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).ratioUnit y y'
      = gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :=
  ((D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).ratioUnit_unique y y'
    (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y')
    (D.component_ratio_eq s 𝒲 σ hσ y y')).symm

/-- The units cocycle of the constructed LocalEquations datum is the (1e) subordinated
cocycle of the datum. -/
lemma sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle :
    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle
      = gluedSubordCocycle D.isGluingCocycle 𝒲 σ hσ :=
  Scheme.unitsCocycle_ext fun y y' =>
    ((D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle_evInf y y').trans
      ((D.sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg y y').trans
        (gluedSubordCocycle_evInf D.isGluingCocycle 𝒲 σ hσ y y').symm)

/-- **THE CLASS LAW** (DAT-A keystone; the Abel correspondence of worksheet §2.2 step
2): the Picard class of the divisor datum cut out by a germ-regular global section of
the DAT-1 glued sheaf is THE Čech Picard class of the datum's cocycle (stage (1e),
consumed on the nose through `cechPicClass_eq_mk`). -/
theorem sectionLocalEquations_picClass :
    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).picClass = D.cechPicClass := by
  change Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒲
    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle.class = D.cechPicClass
  rw [D.sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg]
  exact D.cechPicClass_eq_mk 𝒲 σ hσ

end AffineHom

/-- **Independence of the section and the cover** (refinement/rescaling naturality,
subsumed): the class of the divisor datum cut by ANY germ-regular section of the datum,
on ANY subordinated pointed cover, is the same — both are `D.cechPicClass`. Unit
rescalings and cover refinements of the constructed datum keep the class by the landed
`LocalEquations.picClass_rescale`/`picClass_restrict`. -/
theorem sectionLocalEquations_picClass_congr
    {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
    (s s' : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
    (𝒲 𝒲' : (relCurve C B).PointedCover) (σ σ' : relCurve C B → D.index)
    (hσ : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ y))
    (hσ' : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲'.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ' y))
    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y))
    (hreg' : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s' j)
        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y)) :
    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).picClass
      = (D.sectionLocalEquations s' 𝒲' σ' hσ' hreg').picClass := by
  rw [D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg,
    D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s' 𝒲' σ' hσ' hreg']

/-! ## The A2-bundled wrapper, on the canonical pointed cover -/

section Bundled

variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)

/-- **Fibrewise-nonzero sections cut divisors** (DAT-A + DAT-A2, bundled): over a
Noetherian test ring, a fibrewise-regular global section of the DAT-1 glued sheaf
yields a `LocalEquations` divisor datum on the canonical pointed cover by pieces; its
class is `D.cechPicClass` (`sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_picClass`). -/
noncomputable def sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular
    [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations :=
  D.sectionLocalEquations s D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex (fun _ => le_rfl)
    (fun j y hy => D.germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors s j (hfib j) y hy)

/-- The class law for the A2-bundled wrapper: the fibrewise-regular section cuts a
divisor of class exactly the datum's (1e) class. -/
theorem sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_picClass
    [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    (D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib).picClass = D.cechPicClass :=
  D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex (fun _ => le_rfl) _

end Bundled

end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOnePresentation
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AdmissibleAbelEtaleSurjectiveEffectivity
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The consumed local divisor package for the rank-one route
    11	
    12	This module is the first divisor consumer of PicRankOneLocalPresentation.  The projective
    13	rank-one H0 module supplies a basic open and a section which is nonzero on every residue fibre
    14	there.  The datum-side section construction then gives regular local equations, and the widened
    15	effectivity engine packages those equations as a DivFamZarAff of degree genus C.
    16	
    17	The package is deliberately local and presentation-tied.  It does not define the canonical
    18	family-level divisorOfRankOne, identify the equations with the native zero locus, or assert
    19	that the rank-one locus is represented by an open subscheme.  Those remain the next contracts.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    27	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    28	open scoped TensorProduct
    29	
    30	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    31	
    32	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    33	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    34	
    35	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    36	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    37	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    38	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    39	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
    40	variable {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    41	
    42	namespace PicRankOneLocalPresentation
    43	
    44	/- The degree theorem needs the base-change geometric package under the local relCurve instance,
    45	   which has lower priority in the general curve API. -/
    46	noncomputable local instance (priority := 20000) rankOneLocalDivisorOver
    47	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    48	    (relCurve C L).Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
    49	  instOverBaseChange C L
    50	
    51	noncomputable local instance rankOneLocalDivisorSmooth
    52	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    53	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
    54	  instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
    55	
    56	noncomputable local instance rankOneLocalDivisorIntegral
    57	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    58	    IsIntegral (relCurve C L) :=
    59	  instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
    60	
    61	noncomputable local instance rankOneLocalDivisorQuasiCompact
    62	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    63	    QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
    64	  instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
    65	
    66	noncomputable local instance rankOneLocalDivisorFiniteH0
    67	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    68	    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
    69	  instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
    70	
    71	noncomputable local instance rankOneLocalDivisorFiniteH1
    72	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    73	    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
    74	  instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
    75	
    76	/-! ## Regularity and degree of the local equations -/
    77	
    78	/-- The local equations cut from the tied datum section remain regular after every field-valued
    79	coefficient extension.  This is the regularity input consumed by the widened effectivity
    80	engine, derived from the same fibrewise nonvanishing hypothesis used in the construction. -/
    81	theorem baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations_fibrewiseRegular
    82	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
    83	    [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier]
    84	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)
    85	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
    86	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
    87	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
    88	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
    89	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0)
    90	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    91	    [Algebra (Localization.Away f) L]
    92	    [IsScalarTower k (Localization.Away f) L]
    93	    (z : relCurve C L) :
    94	    ((relCurve C L).presheaf.germ
    95	      (((P.baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations f y hy).cover.pullback
    96	        (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away f) L)).opens z) z
    97	      (((P.baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations f y hy).cover.pullback
    98	        (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away f) L)).mem_opens z)).hom
    99	      (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn
   100	        (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away f) L)
   101	        (P.baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations f y hy) z) ∈
   102	      nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C L).presheaf.stalk z) := by
   103	  let B := Localization.Away f
   104	  let D := P.datum.baseChange B
   105	  let s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤) :=
   106	    P.datumSectionBaseChange B y
   107	  have hsec : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B,
   108	      D.sectionsMapTop q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   109	        (P.datumSectionBaseChange B y) ≠ 0 :=
   110	    fun q => P.sectionsMapTop_datumSectionBaseChange_away_ne_zero f y hy q
   111	  have hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (q : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
   112	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   113	    fun j q => D.injective_rTensor_component_of_sectionsMapTop_ne_zero
   114	      s q (hsec q) j
   115	  unfold baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange
   116	  exact D.germ_self_pullbackEqn_sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular
   117	    s hfib L z
   118	
   119	/-- The local equations have the genus class degree after every field-valued extension.  The
   120	calculation uses the datum class law and datum_classDeg_baseChange, so the degree is tied to
   121	the presentation rather than supplied as an unrelated witness. -/
   122	theorem baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations_classDeg
   123	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   124	    [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier]
   125	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)
   126	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   127	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   128	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   129	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   130	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0)
   131	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   132	    [Algebra (Localization.Away f) L]
   133	    [IsScalarTower k (Localization.Away f) L] :
   134	    classDeg L
   135	      (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away f) L)
   136	        (P.baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations f y hy).picClass) = genus C := by
   137	  letI : Algebra P.cover.Carrier L :=
   138	    ((algebraMap (Localization.Away f) L).comp
   139	      (algebraMap P.cover.Carrier (Localization.Away f))).toAlgebra
   140	  haveI : IsScalarTower P.cover.Carrier (Localization.Away f) L :=
   141	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' rfl
   142	  haveI : IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier L :=
   143	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (by
   144	      rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, RingHom.comp_assoc,
   145	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k P.cover.Carrier (Localization.Away f),
   146	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k (Localization.Away f) L])
   147	  rw [P.baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations_picClass f y hy,
   148	    P.datum.cechPicClass_baseChange (Localization.Away f),
   149	    ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp,
   150	    relCurveMap_comp]
   151	  exact P.datum_classDeg_baseChange L
   152	
   153	/-! ## The local widened divisor and its immediate consumer -/
   154	
   155	/-- The widened divisor cut by a tied rank-one section on its basic open. -/
   156	noncomputable def baseOpenRankOneDivisor
   157	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   158	    [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier]
   159	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)
   160	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   161	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   162	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   163	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   164	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
   165	    DivFamZarAff C (Localization.Away f) (genus C) :=
   166	  divFamZarAffOfFibrewiseRegularLocalEquations C (genus C)
   167	    (P.baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations f y hy) pi
   168	    (P.baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations_fibrewiseRegular f y hy)
   169	    (P.baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations_classDeg f y hy)
   170	
   171	@[simp]
   172	theorem baseOpenRankOneDivisor_picClass
   173	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   174	    [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier]
   175	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)
   176	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   177	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   178	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   179	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   180	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
   181	    (P.baseOpenRankOneDivisor f y hy).picClass =
   182	      (P.datum.baseChange (Localization.Away f)).cechPicClass := by
   183	  unfold baseOpenRankOneDivisor
   184	  rw [picClass_divFamZarAffOfFibrewiseRegularLocalEquations]
   185	  exact P.baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations_picClass f y hy
   186	
   187	/-- The Abel value of the local divisor is the restriction of the input Picard datum.  This is
   188	the immediate consumer which keeps the widened divisor tied to the chosen presentation. -/
   189	theorem baseOpenRankOneDivisor_abelAff
   190	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   191	    [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier]
   192	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)
   193	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   194	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal →

     9	/-!
    10	# The class-indexed witness locus and its openness (the untwisted predecessor of `chartLocus`)
    11	
    12	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusOpen.lean` proves openness of the witness locus of a *chosen*
    13	basic-open cocycle datum `D`; `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean` proves that the witness
    14	predicate is intrinsic to the *fibre class* of the datum.  Both are stated per datum.  This
    15	file makes the step neither takes: it indexes the locus by a **class**.
    16	
    17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.cechWitnessLocus π c` — `{q : Spec B | every basic-open cocycle datum
    18	  with fibre class `c` has an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹` at `κ(q)`}`.
    19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_of_datum` — any ONE presenting datum is a
    20	  sound and complete test (class-intrinsicity).
    21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists` — the ∀-form and the ∃-form agree
    22	  (every class is presented, `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`).
    23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_cechWitnessLocus` — the openness.
    24	
    25	## THIS IS NOT `chartLocus`, AND NOT `isOpen_chartLocus`
    26	
    27	Those two names are RESERVED, and co-signed between two lanes: `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md`
    28	§3.3 (CHART-U(a)) freezes `chartLocus c λ` for a locus over a general test `T`, indexed by a
    29	**plus class** `λ ∈ pic0Subgroup C (Over.mk a)`, at the **twisted** fibre class
    30	`λ_t · θ^m · (−Σ)`; `informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6 co-signs it with two binding
    31	amendments — the predicate for arbitrary plus classes is the SPLIT form over a finite
    32	separable `L/κ(t)`, and the openness route of record is a three-transport chain — and row B-4
    33	owns `isOpen_chartLocus` as the *assembly* of DAT-B's transports (i)/(ii) against DAT-C's
    34	shifted-datum half.  None of that is here.
    35	
    36	What IS here is the step those amendments presuppose and nobody had written: over an affine
    37	base, for an UNTWISTED `CechPic` class, the engine's per-datum output is a locus of the class.
    38	Call it transport (0).  Still missing for `chartLocus` proper: the shifted-datum constructor
    39	(DAT-C GAP-1 — no `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.mul`/tensor exists), the split predicate
    40	(a-amendment), and transports (i) descent and (ii) étale image (DAT-B).
    41	
    42	Free of the DD-R certificate lane and of `divRep`: no `DivFamZar`, no `IsCertified`, no
    43	`RepresentableBy` datum appears in the cone.
    44	-/

    68	/-- **The witness locus of an untwisted class over an affine base**: the set of points of
    69	`Spec B` at which the fibre of the Čech class `c` admits an effective witness divisor with
    70	vanishing `H¹`.
    71	
    72	Stated over *classes*, not over data: a basic-open cocycle datum is a presentation, and the
    73	campaign's consumers index charts by a Picard class.  The ∀-quantifier is harmless because
    74	the predicate is class-intrinsic
    75	(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq`) and every class is
    76	presented (`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`) — see
    77	`mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists`.
    78	
    79	NOT the co-signed `chartLocus c λ` of `w4-datc` §3.3 / `w4-datb` §1.6: that one lives over a
    80	general test, is indexed by a plus class, and reads the TWISTED fibre class.  See the module
    81	header. -/
    82	def cechWitnessLocus (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) : Set (PrimeSpectrum B) :=
    83	  {q : PrimeSpectrum B | ∀ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
    84	    D.cechPicClass = c → D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField}
    85	
    86	theorem mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    87	    q ∈ cechWitnessLocus π c ↔ ∀ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
    88	      D.cechPicClass = c → D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
    89	  Iff.rfl
    90	
    91	/-- **Membership is testable at any one presentation**: a datum `D` presenting `c` is a
    92	sound and complete test for membership of the witness locus.  This is the class-intrinsicity
    93	of the witness predicate, `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq`, in the form
    94	the consumers use. -/
    95	theorem mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_of_datum {c : (relCurve C B).CechPic}
    96	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hD : D.cechPicClass = c) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    97	    q ∈ cechWitnessLocus π c ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
    98	  refine ⟨fun h => h D hD, fun h D' hD' => ?_⟩
    99	  refine (D'.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq D
   100	    q.asIdeal.ResidueField ?_).mpr h
   101	  exact congrArg (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   102	    (hD'.trans hD.symm)
   103	
   104	/-- **The ∀-form and the ∃-form of the witness locus agree**: every class is presented by
   105	some datum, and the witness predicate does not depend on which. -/
   106	theorem mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
   107	    q ∈ cechWitnessLocus π c ↔ ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
   108	      D.cechPicClass = c ∧ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
   109	  obtain ⟨D₀, hD₀⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (π := π) c
   110	  refine ⟨fun h => ⟨D₀, hD₀, h D₀ hD₀⟩, fun ⟨D, hD, h⟩ => ?_⟩
   111	  exact (mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_of_datum D hD q).mpr h
   112	
   113	/-- **The class-indexed witness locus is open**: it is the witness locus of any one
   114	presenting datum, and that is open by
   115	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` (the audited,
   116	Noetherian-free openness engine).
   117	
   118	This is the first *datum-choice-free* openness statement in the campaign — the engine output
   119	is stated for a chosen `D`, which is not something a locus indexed by a Picard class may
   120	depend on.  It is strictly weaker than the reserved `isOpen_chartLocus` (dat-b row B-4),
   121	which assembles this with the shifted-datum constructor and the descent/étale-image
   122	transports; do not cite it as that. -/
   123	theorem isOpen_cechWitnessLocus (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   124	    (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) : IsOpen (cechWitnessLocus π c) := by
   125	  obtain ⟨D₀, hD₀⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (π := π) c
   126	  have hset : cechWitnessLocus π c
   127	      = {q : PrimeSpectrum B |
   128	          ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
   129	            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
   130	                = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   131	                    D₀.cechPicClass
   132	              ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   133	                  ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
   134	                    q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} :=
   135	    Set.ext fun q => mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_of_datum D₀ hD₀ q
   136	  rw [hset]
   137	  exact D₀.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing hπ
   138	
   139	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	/-!
    10	# The presentation locus for the rank-one Abel map
    11	
    12	`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
    13	every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine
    14	pullback makes the condition intrinsic on arbitrary test schemes; stability under further
    15	pullback is exactly `picEtMap_comp`.
    16	
    17	The remaining declarations form the corresponding preimages in the widened divisor functor and
    18	in its canonical representing Yoneda functor, together with the restricted Abel transformations.
    19	These are logical subfunctors only.  In particular, this file does not prove that
    20	`PicRankOneOpen` is represented by an open subscheme, and it reserves `DivRankOneOpen` for the
    21	future actual open subscheme of the divisor representer.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    30	
    31	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    32	
    33	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    34	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    35	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    36	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	/-- The rank-one presentation locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer.
    41	
    42	Membership means that every affine pullback of the input plus class admits a local presentation
    43	tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
    44	locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
    45	def PicRankOneOpen :
    46	    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
    47	  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    48	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    49	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    50	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}
    51	  map {T T'} f lam hlam A _ _ t := by
    52	    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)
    53	    have e : F.map t.op (F.map f lam) = F.map (t ≫ f.unop).op lam := by
    54	      apply Subtype.ext
    55	      exact (picEtMap_comp C f.unop t lam.1).symm
    56	    rw [e]
    57	    exact hlam A (t ≫ f.unop)
    58	
    59	/-- The inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` under the affine widened Abel transformation.
    60	
    61	This name deliberately records only a presentation-theoretic preimage.  It is not the future
    62	open subscheme `DivRankOneOpen`. -/
    63	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff :
    64	    Subfunctor (divFunctorAff C (genus C)) :=
    65	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).preimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
    66	
    67	/-- The same presentation preimage on the Yoneda functor of the canonical genus divisor
    68	representer. -/
    69	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter :
    70	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
    71	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).preimage
    72	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
    73	
    74	/-- The affine Abel transformation restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
    75	def rankOneAbelAff :
    76	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor ⟶
    77	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
    78	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).fromPreimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
    79	
    80	/-- Restrict the canonical representation isomorphism to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
    81	def rankOneRepresenterRestriction :
    82	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
    83	      (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor :=
    84	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).fromPreimage
    85	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
    86	
    87	/-- The represented genus Abel map restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
    88	def rankOneAbelRepresented :
    89	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
    90	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
    91	  rankOneRepresenterRestriction pi ≫ rankOneAbelAff pi
    92	
    93	end
    94	
    95	end AlgebraicGeometry

     8	/-!
     9	# CHART-U(b) — datum-level openness of the chart-membership (witness) locus
    10	(`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6, `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3)
    11	
    12	The affine-level heart of the shared CHART-U(b) brick, stated directly on a pinned
    13	basic-open cocycle datum in the **witness form** the `chartLocus` predicate uses.
    14	
    15	For a datum `D` over an affine base `B`, the locus of primes `q` of `B` at which the
    16	fibre class of `D` at `κ(q)` admits an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`
    17	is Zariski-open in `Spec B`.  This is the single sanctioned openness mechanism of the
    18	campaign (`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing`, Noetherian-free — dat-d §3.5) read
    19	through the two-way datum dictionary of C1
    20	(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness`,
    21	`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-6): the engine open is the complex-form fibre
    22	condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗[B] κ(q))`, and the dictionary rewrites it,
    23	pointwise and class-intrinsically, as the effective-witness/h¹-vanishing condition.
    24	
    25	Role in the CHART-U(b) chain (the two unlanded links of §5 risk 1):
    26	
    27	* **the shifted-datum constructor (link 1):** over the étale carrier `B` the plus
    28	  class collapses to an honest Čech class; twisted by the theta layer and DAT-C's
    29	  GAP-1 inverse datum into the `λθᵐ(Σ-shift)⁻¹` class, then extracted
    30	  (`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`) to a datum `D`.  The output of
    31	  that link is exactly a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` — the input of the theorem
    32	  below, whose witness set is then the `chartLocus`-over-`B`.
    33	* **the étale-image openness transport (link 2):** the locus over the test base `A`
    34	  is the image, under the (open, surjective) étale carrier map `Spec B → Spec A`, of
    35	  the open locus this theorem produces — carried to `A` by mathlib's
    36	  `IsOpenMap.isQuotientMap`/`IsQuotientMap.isOpen_preimage` once the fibre-field
    37	  invariance identifies the preimage.
    38	
    39	The theorem is class-intrinsic (any datum in the class has the same witness set, by
    40	(V1a)), so a change of extracted representative is free.
    41	-/
    42	
    43	set_option autoImplicit false
    44	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
    45	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

    58	open AlgebraicJacobian

    60	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    61	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    62	
    63	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    64	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    65	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
    66	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    67	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    68	
    69	/-- **CHART-U(b), the datum-level witness-locus openness** (`w4-datc` §3.3 step (3)):
    70	for a pinned basic-open cocycle datum `D` over the affine base `B`, the locus of primes
    71	`q` at which the fibre class of `D` at `κ(q)` has an effective witness divisor with
    72	vanishing `H¹` is open in `Spec B`.

    74	This is `datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` (the single audited openness engine,
    75	Noetherian-free) read in the class/witness form of the `chartLocus` predicate through
    76	the two-way datum dictionary
    77	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (C1, GAP-6):
    78	pointwise the engine's complex-form condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗[B] κ(q))`
    79	is exactly the existence of such a witness. -/
    80	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing
    81	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) :
    82	    IsOpen {q : PrimeSpectrum B |
    83	      ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
    84	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
    85	            = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass
    86	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    87	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
    88	                q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} := by

    90	      ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
    91	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
    92	            = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass
    93	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    94	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
    95	                q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)}
    96	      = {p : PrimeSpectrum B |
    97	          Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)} := by
    98	    refine Set.ext fun q => ?_
    99	    exact (D.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness q.asIdeal.ResidueField).symm
   100	  rw [hset]
   101	  exact datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing D hπ

   103	/-! ## The openness transport (CHART-U(b) link 2, topological half)
   104	
   105	The engine produces the open witness locus over the étale carrier `Spec B` (or, on the
   106	away pieces, over `Spec (Localization.Away f)`).  CHART-U(b)'s transport (ii)
   107	(`w4-datb` §1.6, "the Kleiman tex 2204-2244 step, now one `IsOpenMap` application")
   108	carries it down to the test base `Spec A` along the étale carrier map, which is open
   109	and surjective.  The pure-topology core of that step is below; the remaining
   110	mathematical content of link 2 is the *fibre-field invariance* that identifies the

   112	`isH1VanishingAt_comap_away_iff` is the landed avatar for the away case). -/

   115	open, and surjective and `f ⁻¹' V` is open, then `V` is open — because
   116	`V = f '' (f ⁻¹' V)` (surjectivity) and `f` carries opens to opens.  This is the
   117	topological core of CHART-U(b)'s transport (ii). -/
   118	theorem isOpen_of_isOpen_preimage_of_isOpenMap_surjective
   119	    {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] {f : X → Y}
   120	    (hcont : Continuous f) (hopen : IsOpenMap f) (hsurj : Function.Surjective f)
   121	    {V : Set Y} (hV : IsOpen (f ⁻¹' V)) : IsOpen V :=
   122	  ((hopen.isQuotientMap hcont hsurj).isOpen_preimage).mp hV
   123

   125	half): for a ring map `f : R →+* S` whose induced `Spec S → Spec R` is open and
   126	surjective (e.g. an étale carrier map), a locus of `Spec R` whose preimage in `Spec S`
   127	is open is itself open.  The engine's open witness locus lives on the carrier `Spec S`;
   128	this pushes it to the test base `Spec R`. -/
   129	theorem isOpen_of_isOpen_comap_preimage {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
   130	    (f : R →+* S) (hopen : IsOpenMap (PrimeSpectrum.comap f))
   131	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap f))
   132	    {V : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)} (hV : IsOpen (PrimeSpectrum.comap f ⁻¹' V)) :
   133	    IsOpen V :=
   134	  isOpen_of_isOpen_preimage_of_isOpenMap_surjective
   135	    (PrimeSpectrum.continuous_comap f) hopen hsurj hV
   136	
   137	end AlgebraicGeometry

    12	/-!
    13	# Invertible sections of a cocycle-glued line bundle on an affine open
    14	
    15	The cocycle pieces used to construct `gluedSheaf` need not contain an arbitrary affine
    16	open.  Nevertheless, every affine open admits a finite basic-open refinement subordinate
    17	to the canonical pointed cover by those pieces.  On each refined basic open the glued
    18	sheaf is free of rank one.  The existing localization-span engine then proves that its
    19	sections on the original affine open are finite projective.
    20	
    21	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.AffineSectionsModel` packages the quasi-coherent action chosen by
    22	that internal refinement together with the finite, projective, and invertible instances.
    23	Returning a `Nonempty` model keeps the refinement choice noncomputable while giving
    24	downstream code a single datum from which it can install all four compatible instances.
    25	
    26	This is the chart-free line-bundle substrate needed to restrict a positive theta twist to
    27	the arbitrary affine pieces of `AffAdaptation`: the divisor cover is not required to lie in
    28	either pinned theta chart.
    29	-/
    30	
    31	set_option autoImplicit false
    32	
    33	universe u
    34	
    35	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    36	open scoped TensorProduct
    37	
    38	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    39	
    40	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule
    41	
    42	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    43	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    44	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
    45	
    46	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
    47	
    48	/-- A compatible quasi-coherent module structure on the sections of a cocycle-glued
    49	line bundle over an affine open, together with its finite projective rank-one properties.
    50	
    51	The module instance is written explicitly in the fields so that it is definitionally the
    52	one induced by `qcoh`; a consumer may install `M.qcoh` and recover `M.finite` and
    53	`M.projective` without any proof-irrelevance transport. -/
    54	structure AffineSectionsModel (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    55	    (V : (relCurve C B).Opens) where
    56	  qcoh : Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf V
    57	  qsmul_eq : ∀ {W : (relCurve C B).Opens} (hWV : W ≤ V) (r : Γ(relCurve C B, V))
    58	      (s : D.sheaf.obj.obj (op W)),
    59	      letI := qcoh
    60	      Scheme.QcohOn.qsmul (F := D.sheaf) hWV r s =
    61	        gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit hWV r s
    62	  finite : @Module.Finite Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))
    63	    _ _ (@Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE B _ (relCurve C B) V D.sheaf qcoh V (le_refl V))
    64	  projective : @Module.Projective Γ(relCurve C B, V) _
    65	    (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) _
    66	    (@Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE B _ (relCurve C B) V D.sheaf qcoh V (le_refl V))
    67	  invertible : @Module.Invertible Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))
    68	    _ _ (@Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE B _ (relCurve C B) V D.sheaf qcoh V (le_refl V))
    69	
    70	/-- Sections of a cocycle-glued line bundle on every affine open admit a compatible
    71	invertible module model.  The proof chooses a finite basic-open refinement of the canonical
    72	pointed cover, trivializes after the resulting faithfully flat product localization, and
    73	descends invertibility; finiteness and projectivity are recorded on the same action. -/
    74	theorem nonempty_affineSectionsModel (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    75	    (V : (relCurve C B).Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
    76	    Nonempty (D.AffineSectionsModel V) := by
    77	  classical
    78	  obtain ⟨ι, fint, f, anchor, coeff, hP, hpart⟩ :=
    79	    hV.exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement D.pointedCover
    80	  letI : Fintype ι := fint
    81	  let sigma : ι → D.index := fun i => D.pieceIndex (anchor i)
    82	  have hP' : ∀ i : ι, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i) ≤ D.pieces (sigma i) := hP
    83	  have hcov : V ≤ ⨆ i : ι, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i) :=
    84	    le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one coeff f hpart
    85	  let q : Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf V :=

    11	
    12	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, this file views an `X.Modules` object as a sheaf of
    13	`k`-modules.  The construction keeps the same section types and restriction maps; only the
    14	scalar action is restricted along `k -> Gamma(X, U)`.  It is the dialect bridge needed to
    15	compare a `Scheme.Modules` line bundle with the fixed-base module sheaves used by the Cech
    16	cohomology engine.

    21	universe u

    27	variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k]

    29	/-- The base-ring module structure on sections of a scheme module. -/

    31	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules)
    32	    (U : X.left.Opens) : Module k Γ(M, U) :=
    33	  Module.compHom _ (X.left.overAlgebraMap k U)

    46	    X.left.Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} k where

    10	/-!
    11	# Sections to divisors — the DAT-A2 germ-regularity bridge
    12	
    13	The geometry layer of the `lm:ctn` (iii)⟹(i) slicing criterion
    14	(`informal/spec-dat-a.md` §2; core: `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FibrewiseRegular`):
    15	
    16	* **(α) germ transport** — `IsAffineOpen.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors`: a nonzerodivisor of
    17	  the section ring of an affine open has nonzerodivisor germs at all of its points
    18	  (stalks are localizations of the affine section ring; regularity passes to
    19	  localizations). This is also the "germ-level regularity by localization-exactness"
    20	  consumption surface of DD-1a (dat-d-worksheet §1.2).
    21	* **(the field-level slice case, Kleiman tex 2013–2022)** —
    22	  `Scheme.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero`: on an **integral** scheme a nonzero
    23	  section has nonzerodivisor germs everywhere on its open. This is the named lemma
    24	  DAT-C discharges at field-level fibres ("nonzero on the integral fibre ⟹ regular").
    25	* **(β) piece flatness** — `flat_sections_basicOpen`: over `Spec k`, if the affine
    26	  chart ring is `k`-flat (`Scheme.overModule`) then so is every basic-open piece ring
    27	  (tower `k → Γ(V) → Γ(D(h))` through `IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen`).
    28	* **(γ) the generic A2 bridge** — `mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_fibrewise_regular` (+ germ
    29	  form): over a Noetherian `k`, a section of a basic-open piece of a `k`-flat affine
    30	  chart that is **fibrewise regular** (multiplication injective on every residue-field
    31	  fibre of the piece ring, in `Scheme.mulSectionEnd`/`rTensor` form) is a nonzerodivisor
    32	  with nonzerodivisor germs. The tensor-RING form of the fibre hypothesis converts
    33	  through `injective_rTensor_mulSectionEnd_of_tmul_mem_nonZeroDivisors`.
    34	* **(δ) A2 on the pinned datum** — for `D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` and a global
    35	  section `s` of the DAT-1 glued sheaf, each component `D.component s j` (the section on
    36	  the trivializing basic-open piece `D(h_j)`) is a nonzerodivisor with nonzerodivisor
    37	  germs, given its fibrewise regularity (`component_mem_nonZeroDivisors`,
    38	  `germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors`). These are exactly the `regular` inputs of
    39	  `Scheme.LocalEquations` — the LocalEquations construction and the class law are in
    40	  `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionsToDivisorsClass`.
    41	
    42	The fibrewise hypothesis is deliberately the *piece-ring residue-fibre* spelling
    43	(worksheet §2.2.2 with §5 risk 4 discharged): it is vacuous on pieces missing a fibre
    44	(zero ring), it is exactly what the integral-fibre slice case produces where the fibre
    45	ring is a domain, and it keeps the un-landed 1d-ii/DAT-3 fibre-sheaf identifications
    46	with their owners (DAT-C/DD-R bridge their fibre-curve statements to this spelling).
    47	-/

    59	/-! ## `nonZeroDivisors` ↔ `IsSMulRegular` on a commutative ring -/
    60	
    61	section Bridges
    62	
    63	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    64	
    65	/-- A nonzerodivisor of a commutative ring is a regular element for the
    66	self-multiplication action. -/
    67	theorem isSMulRegular_self_of_mem_nonZeroDivisors {t : A}
    68	    (ht : t ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) : IsSMulRegular A t := by
    69	  intro u v huv
    70	  have h0 : (u - v) * t = 0 := by
    71	    have hm : t * u = t * v := huv
    72	    rw [sub_mul, mul_comm u, mul_comm v, hm, sub_self]
    73	  exact sub_eq_zero.mp ((mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff.mp ht).2 (u - v) h0)
    74	
    75	/-- A regular element for the self-multiplication action of a commutative ring is a
    76	nonzerodivisor. -/
    77	theorem mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isSMulRegular_self {t : A}
    78	    (h : IsSMulRegular A t) : t ∈ nonZeroDivisors A := by
    79	  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff]
    80	  refine ⟨fun z hz => ?_, fun z hz => ?_⟩
    81	  · refine h (show t • z = t • 0 by
    82	      rw [smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul, mul_zero]; exact hz)
    83	  · refine h (show t • z = t • 0 by
    84	      rw [smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul, mul_zero, mul_comm]; exact hz)
    85	
    86	end Bridges

    88	/-! ## (α) Germ transport on an affine open, and the field-level slice case -/
    89	
    90	section Germ
    91	
    92	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
    93	
    94	/-- **Germ transport on an affine open**: a nonzerodivisor of `Γ(X, U)` has
    95	nonzerodivisor germs at every point of `U`. The stalk is the localization of the affine
    96	section ring at the point's prime (`IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_stalk`), and regularity
    97	passes to localizations. -/
    98	theorem IsAffineOpen.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    99	    {t : Γ(X, U)} (ht : t ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, U)) (y : X) (hy : y ∈ U) :
   100	    (X.presheaf.germ U y hy).hom t ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y) := by
   101	  letI : Algebra Γ(X, U) (X.presheaf.stalk y) :=
   102	    X.presheaf.algebra_section_stalk ⟨y, hy⟩
   103	  haveI := hU.isLocalization_stalk ⟨y, hy⟩
   104	  have hreg : IsSMulRegular (X.presheaf.stalk y)
   105	      (algebraMap Γ(X, U) (X.presheaf.stalk y) t) :=
   106	    (isSMulRegular_self_of_mem_nonZeroDivisors ht).of_isLocalization
   107	      (X.presheaf.stalk y) (hU.primeIdealOf ⟨y, hy⟩).asIdeal.primeCompl
   108	  exact mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isSMulRegular_self hreg
   109	
   110	/-- **The field-level slice case** (Kleiman tex 2013–2022, "`σ_t ≠ 0` on the integral
   111	fibre, hence `σ_t` is regular"): on an integral scheme, a nonzero section has
   112	nonzerodivisor germs at every point of its open. Named separately for DAT-C's canonical
   113	-section normalization at field-level fibres. -/
   114	theorem Scheme.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero [IsIntegral X]
   115	    {U : X.Opens} {t : Γ(X, U)} (ht : t ≠ 0) (y : X) (hy : y ∈ U) :
   116	    (X.presheaf.germ U y hy).hom t ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y) := by
   117	  refine mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero (fun h0 => ht ?_)
   118	  exact germ_injective_of_isIntegral X y hy (by rw [h0, map_zero])
   119	
   120	end Germ

   122	/-! ## (β) Piece flatness and (γ) the generic A2 bridge -/
   123	
   124	section Piece
   125	
   126	variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
   127	
   128	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule
   129	
   130	/-- **Piece flatness**: if the section ring of an affine open `V` is a flat `k`-module
   131	(`Scheme.overModule`), then so is the section ring of every basic open `D(h) ⊆ V` —
   132	the tower `k → Γ(V) → Γ(D(h))` with `Γ(D(h))` a localization of `Γ(V)`.
   133	`private`: the public copy (same content, binder order `hV hflat f`) lives in
   134	`DivSchemeFamilySide` — same-day concurrent coinage (the I-0190 pattern), collision
   135	surfaced at the first full root build; external consumers use that copy. -/
   136	private theorem flat_sections_basicOpen {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (h : Γ(X, V))
   137	    (hflat : Module.Flat k Γ(X, V)) :
   138	    Module.Flat k Γ(X, X.basicOpen h) := by
   139	  letI : Algebra k Γ(X, V) := (X.overAlgebraMap k V).toAlgebra
   140	  letI : Algebra k Γ(X, X.basicOpen h) :=
   141	    (X.overAlgebraMap k (X.basicOpen h)).toAlgebra
   142	  haveI : IsLocalization.Away h Γ(X, X.basicOpen h) := hV.isLocalization_basicOpen h
   143	  haveI : Module.Flat Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen h) :=
   144	    IsLocalization.flat _ (Submonoid.powers h)
   145	  haveI : Module.Flat k Γ(X, V) := hflat
   146	  haveI : IsScalarTower k Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen h) :=
   147	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq'
   148	      (X.overAlgebraMap_naturality k (homOfLE (X.basicOpen_le h)).op).symm
   149	  exact Module.Flat.trans k Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen h)
   150	
   151	/-- **The generic A2 bridge** (`lm:ctn` (iii)⟹(i) on a basic-open piece of a flat
   152	affine chart): over a Noetherian `k`, a section `t` of `D(h) ⊆ V` whose multiplication
   153	endomorphism is injective on every residue-field fibre of the piece ring is a
   154	nonzerodivisor. -/
   155	theorem mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_fibrewise_regular [IsNoetherianRing k]
   156	    {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (h : Γ(X, V))
   157	    (hflat : Module.Flat k Γ(X, V)) (t : Γ(X, X.basicOpen h))
   158	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum k, Function.Injective
   159	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd k t).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   160	    t ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, X.basicOpen h) := by
   161	  haveI : Module.Flat k Γ(X, X.basicOpen h) := flat_sections_basicOpen k hV h hflat
   162	  have hinj : Function.Injective (Scheme.mulSectionEnd k t) :=
   163	    Module.Flat.injective_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective
   164	      (Scheme.mulSectionEnd k t) hfib
   165	  refine mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isSMulRegular_self (fun u v huv => hinj ?_)
   166	  rw [Scheme.mulSectionEnd_apply, Scheme.mulSectionEnd_apply]
   167	  exact huv
   168	
   169	/-- The germ form of the generic A2 bridge: fibrewise-regular sections of basic-open
   170	pieces have nonzerodivisor germs (feeds `Scheme.LocalEquations.regular`). -/
   171	theorem germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_fibrewise_regular [IsNoetherianRing k]
   172	    {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (h : Γ(X, V))
   173	    (hflat : Module.Flat k Γ(X, V)) (t : Γ(X, X.basicOpen h))
   174	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum k, Function.Injective
   175	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd k t).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   176	    (y : X) (hy : y ∈ X.basicOpen h) :
   177	    (X.presheaf.germ (X.basicOpen h) y hy).hom t
   178	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y) :=
   179	  (hV.basicOpen h).germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors
   180	    (mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_fibrewise_regular k hV h hflat t hfib) y hy
   181	
   182	/-- Conversion from the tensor-RING spelling of the fibre hypothesis (`t ⊗ 1` a
   183	nonzerodivisor of the piece-ring fibre `Γ(W) ⊗[k] κ(p)`) to the `rTensor` spelling the
   184	A2 bridge consumes. The `k`-algebra structure on the section ring is the structure
   185	morphism (`Scheme.overAlgebraMap`), whose module structure is `Scheme.overModule` on
   186	the nose. -/
   187	theorem injective_rTensor_mulSectionEnd_of_tmul_mem_nonZeroDivisors
   188	    {W : X.Opens} (t : Γ(X, W)) (p : PrimeSpectrum k)
   189	    (hfib : letI : Algebra k Γ(X, W) := (X.overAlgebraMap k W).toAlgebra
   190	      (t ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   191	          Γ(X, W) ⊗[k] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
   192	        nonZeroDivisors (Γ(X, W) ⊗[k] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   193	    Function.Injective
   194	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd k t).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
   195	  letI : Algebra k Γ(X, W) := (X.overAlgebraMap k W).toAlgebra
   196	  have hend : Scheme.mulSectionEnd k t = LinearMap.mulLeft k t := by
   197	    ext s
   198	    simp [Scheme.mulSectionEnd_apply]
   199	  rw [hend, rTensor_mulLeft_eq_mulLeft_tmul p.asIdeal.ResidueField t]
   200	  intro u v huv
   201	  have hzero : (u - v) * (t ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) = 0 := by
   202	    rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply] at huv
   203	    rw [sub_mul, mul_comm u, mul_comm v, huv, sub_self]
   204	  exact sub_eq_zero.mp ((mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff.mp hfib).2 (u - v) hzero)
   205	
   206	end Piece

   208	/-! ## (δ) A2 on the pinned cocycle datum -/
   209	
   210	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
   211	
   212	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule
   213	
   214	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   215	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
   216	
   217	section AffineHom
   218	
   219	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
   220	variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
   221	
   222	/-- The `j`-th **component** of a global section of the datum's glued sheaf, as a
   223	section of the trivializing basic-open piece `D(h_j)` (the `⊤ ⊓ pieces j`-to-`pieces j`
   224	restriction of the matching family's `j`-th entry). -/
   225	noncomputable def component (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
   226	    (j : D.index) : Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) :=
   227	  (relCurve C B).resHom (le_inf le_top le_rfl) (s.val j)
   228	
   229	/-- Every piece of the pinned datum is an affine open (a basic open of a pinned affine
   230	chart). -/
   231	theorem isAffineOpen_pieces (j : D.index) : IsAffineOpen (D.pieces j) := by
   232	  cases j with
   233	  | inl j₀ => exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen (D.h₀ j₀)
   234	  | inr j₁ => exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen (D.h₁ j₁)
   235	
   236	end AffineHom
   237	
   238	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
   239	variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
   240	
   241	/-- **DAT-A2 on the datum, section-ring form**: a fibrewise-regular component of a
   242	global section of the DAT-1 glued sheaf is a nonzerodivisor of its piece ring
   243	(fibrewise-regular + flat ⟹ regular; the chart rings are free `B`-modules by
   244	`free_relSections`, so the pieces are flat, and the `lm:ctn`-lite core fires). -/
   245	theorem component_mem_nonZeroDivisors [IsNoetherianRing B]
   246	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤)) (j : D.index)
   247	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, Function.Injective
   248	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   249	    D.component s j ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) := by
   250	  cases j with
   251	  | inl j₀ =>
   252	      haveI : Module.Free B Γ(relCurve C B, (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀) :=
   253	        free_relSections C B (fiberChart₀ π)
   254	          (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0).isCompact
   255	          (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0).isQuasiSeparated
   256	      exact mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_fibrewise_regular B
   257	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B (fiberTwoCover π)) (D.h₀ j₀)
   258	        Module.Flat.of_free (D.component s (Sum.inl j₀)) hfib
   259	  | inr j₁ =>
   260	      haveI : Module.Free B Γ(relCurve C B, (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁) :=
   261	        free_relSections C B (fiberChart₁ π)
   262	          (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1).isCompact
   263	          (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1).isQuasiSeparated
   264	      exact mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_fibrewise_regular B
   265	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B (fiberTwoCover π)) (D.h₁ j₁)
   266	        Module.Flat.of_free (D.component s (Sum.inr j₁)) hfib
   267	
   268	/-- **DAT-A2 on the datum, germ form** (the `Scheme.LocalEquations.regular` input): a
   269	fibrewise-regular component has nonzerodivisor germs at every point of its piece. -/
   270	theorem germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors [IsNoetherianRing B]
   271	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤)) (j : D.index)
   272	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, Function.Injective
   273	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   274	    (y : ↑(relCurve C B).toPresheafedSpace) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j) :
   275	    ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
   276	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y) :=
   277	  (D.isAffineOpen_pieces j).germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors
   278	    (D.component_mem_nonZeroDivisors s j hfib) y hy
   279	
   280	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

events.text: The code already contains the categorical Beck–Chevalley identity, so another restatement would not move the gate. I found a more direct route toward canonicity: exploit that two local generators of the rank-one \(H^0\) module differ by a unit, then prove their tied divisor packages are equal in the `DivEq` quotient; this is the choice-independence needed to glue `divisorOfRankOne`.

1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors. All rights reserved.
     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import Mathlib.RingTheory.TensorProduct.Basic
     7	import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Tower
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Units from evaluated trivialization generators
    11	
    12	For a trivialization `t : R ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[R] R` of a base-changed module, the generator
    13	`t.symm 1` generates `R ⊗[A] M` as an `R`-module.  This file proves the abstract
    14	unit-production lemma of the ζ3 kernel-lemma construction: pushing the generator along
    15	a ring map `φ : R → R'` (as `rTensor` of an `A`-linear avatar of `φ`) and applying any
    16	surjective `R'`-linear evaluation `F : R' ⊗[A] M →ₗ[R'] R'` yields a **unit** of `R'`
    17	(`Module.isUnit_map_rTensor_generator`).
    18	
    19	It also packages the multiplication evaluation `Module.descentMulEval`: for a tower
    20	`A → B' → R'` and a descent equivalence `dE : B' ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[B'] B'`, the base-changed
    21	`R'`-linear equivalence `R' ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[R'] R'` with `r' ⊗ m ↦ r' * algebraMap _ _ (dE
    22	(1 ⊗ m))` — the concrete surjective evaluation fed to the unit-production lemma.
    23	
    24	Everything is stated over abstract commutative rings so that the kernel checks small
    25	types; the composite section-ring instance stacks appear only at the single
    26	instantiation site in `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DescentClassRepBuild`.
    27	-/
    28	
    29	set_option autoImplicit false
    30	
    31	universe u
    32	
    33	open scoped TensorProduct
    34	
    35	namespace Module
    36	
    37	variable {A R R' M : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing R] [CommRing R']
    38	  [Algebra A R] [Algebra A R'] [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    39	
    40	/-- The generator property of a trivialization: every element is the `t`-value scalar
    41	multiple of the generator `t.symm 1`. -/
    42	lemma trivialization_smul_symm_one {M₀ : Type u} [AddCommGroup M₀] [Module R M₀]
    43	    (t : M₀ ≃ₗ[R] R) (x : M₀) :
    44	    t x • t.symm 1 = x := by
    45	  apply t.injective
    46	  rw [map_smul, LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    47	
    48	/-- `rTensor` of an `A`-linear avatar of a ring map is `φ`-semilinear for the
    49	module-side scalars. -/
    50	lemma rTensor_smul_of_ringHom (φ : R →+* R') (φₗ : R →ₗ[A] R')
    51	    (hφ : ∀ r, φₗ r = φ r) (c : R) (x : R ⊗[A] M) :
    52	    LinearMap.rTensor M φₗ (c • x) = φ c • LinearMap.rTensor M φₗ x := by
    53	  induction x with
    54	  | zero => rw [smul_zero, map_zero, smul_zero]
    55	  | tmul r m =>
    56	      rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, LinearMap.rTensor_tmul,
    57	        LinearMap.rTensor_tmul, TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, hφ, hφ, map_mul]
    58	  | add x y hx hy => rw [smul_add, map_add, hx, hy, map_add, smul_add]
    59	
    60	/-- **Unit production from an evaluated generator**: pushing the (collapsed) generator
    61	of a trivialization `t : M' ≃ₗ[R] R` along `φ : R → R'` (through a collapse
    62	`cN : M' ≃ₗ[R] R ⊗[A] M`) and evaluating by any surjective `R'`-linear map
    63	`R' ⊗[A] M → R'` produces a unit of `R'`. -/
    64	theorem isUnit_map_rTensor_generator (φ : R →+* R') (φₗ : R →ₗ[A] R')
    65	    (hφ : ∀ r, φₗ r = φ r) {M' : Type u} [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M']
    66	    (t : M' ≃ₗ[R] R) (cN : M' ≃ₗ[R] R ⊗[A] M)
    67	    (F : R' ⊗[A] M →ₗ[R'] R') (hF : Function.Surjective F) :
    68	    IsUnit (F (LinearMap.rTensor M φₗ (cN (t.symm 1)))) := by
    69	  -- every element of `R ⊗[A] M` is an `R`-multiple of the collapsed generator
    70	  have hgen₀ : ∀ x : R ⊗[A] M, x = t (cN.symm x) • cN (t.symm 1) := by
    71	    intro x
    72	    rw [← map_smul, trivialization_smul_symm_one, LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
    73	  -- every element of `R' ⊗[A] M` is an `R'`-multiple of the pushed generator
    74	  have hgen : ∀ z : R' ⊗[A] M,
    75	      ∃ c : R', z = c • LinearMap.rTensor M φₗ (cN (t.symm 1)) := by
    76	    intro z
    77	    induction z with
    78	    | zero => exact ⟨0, (zero_smul _ _).symm⟩
    79	    | tmul r' m =>
    80	        refine ⟨r' * φ (t (cN.symm ((1 : R) ⊗ₜ[A] m))), ?_⟩
    81	        have h1 : LinearMap.rTensor M φₗ ((1 : R) ⊗ₜ[A] m) = (1 : R') ⊗ₜ[A] m := by
    82	          rw [LinearMap.rTensor_tmul, hφ, map_one]
    83	        calc r' ⊗ₜ[A] m
    84	            = r' • ((1 : R') ⊗ₜ[A] m) := by
    85	              rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    86	          _ = r' • LinearMap.rTensor M φₗ ((1 : R) ⊗ₜ[A] m) := by rw [h1]
    87	          _ = r' • LinearMap.rTensor M φₗ
    88	                (t (cN.symm ((1 : R) ⊗ₜ[A] m)) • cN (t.symm 1)) := by
    89	              rw [← hgen₀]
    90	          _ = r' • (φ (t (cN.symm ((1 : R) ⊗ₜ[A] m)))
    91	                • LinearMap.rTensor M φₗ (cN (t.symm 1))) := by
    92	              rw [rTensor_smul_of_ringHom φ φₗ hφ]
    93	          _ = (r' * φ (t (cN.symm ((1 : R) ⊗ₜ[A] m))))
    94	                • LinearMap.rTensor M φₗ (cN (t.symm 1)) := by
    95	              rw [smul_smul]
    96	    | add x y hx hy =>
    97	        obtain ⟨c₁, hc₁⟩ := hx
    98	        obtain ⟨c₂, hc₂⟩ := hy
    99	        exact ⟨c₁ + c₂, by rw [hc₁, hc₂, add_smul]⟩
   100	  -- pull `1` back through `F` and rewrite via the generator property
   101	  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hF 1
   102	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hgen y
   103	  refine IsUnit.of_mul_eq_one c ?_
   104	  rw [mul_comm, ← smul_eq_mul, ← map_smul, ← hc, hy]
   105	
   106	/-! ## The multiplication evaluation of a descent equivalence -/
   107	
   108	variable (A M) in
   109	/-- The base change of a descent equivalence `B' ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[B'] B'` along `B' → R'`,
   110	collapsed to an `R'`-linear equivalence `R' ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[R'] R'`. -/
   111	noncomputable def descentMulEval {B' : Type u} [CommRing B'] [Algebra A B']
   112	    [Algebra B' R'] [IsScalarTower A B' R'] (dE : B' ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[B'] B') :
   113	    (R' ⊗[A] M) ≃ₗ[R'] R' :=
   114	  (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange A B' R' R' M).symm ≪≫ₗ
   115	    TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.congr (LinearEquiv.refl R' R') dE ≪≫ₗ
   116	      TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.rid B' R' R'
   117	
   118	lemma descentMulEval_tmul {B' : Type u} [CommRing B'] [Algebra A B']
   119	    [Algebra B' R'] [IsScalarTower A B' R'] (dE : B' ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[B'] B')
   120	    (r' : R') (m : M) :
   121	    descentMulEval A M dE (r' ⊗ₜ[A] m) = dE ((1 : B') ⊗ₜ[A] m) • r' := by
   122	  have h1 : (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange A B' R' R' M).symm
   123	      (r' ⊗ₜ[A] m) = r' ⊗ₜ[B'] ((1 : B') ⊗ₜ[A] m) := by
   124	    rw [LinearEquiv.symm_apply_eq,
   125	      TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange_tmul, one_smul]
   126	  rw [descentMulEval, LinearEquiv.trans_apply, LinearEquiv.trans_apply, h1,
   127	    TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.congr_tmul, LinearEquiv.refl_apply,
   128	    TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.rid_tmul]
   129	
   130	end Module

    11	# DAT-C C4 — the canonical-section normalization mono (N4/N5 + the local-basis companion)
    12	(`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §2 (N4)/(N5), GAP-3 companion)
    13	
    14	This file provides the module-theoretic heart of the canonical-section normalization —
    15	the deferred GAP-3 **Nakayama companion** (I-0253): a *given* fibrewise-nonzero element of
    16	a rank-`1` finite projective module is a **Zariski-local basis** (the converse direction
    17	of N3's generator production) — together with the DAT-A class law N4 for arbitrary
    18	fibrewise-regular sections of the divisor datum.
    19	
    20	* `Module.exists_notMem_bijective_toSpanSingleton` — **the Nakayama companion** (GAP-3
    21	  companion, deferred from C2/I-0253): for a finite projective `B`-module `Q` of
    22	  stalk-rank `1` at `p` and an element `q` nonzero in the fibre `Q ⊗ κ(p)`, there is a
    23	  basic open `D(f) ∋ p` on which `x ↦ x • q` is a **bijection** `B_f → Q_f`, i.e. `q`
    24	  is a local basis of `Q`.  Route: over the local ring `Rₚ` the localized module `Qₚ` is
    25	  free of rank `1`; the fibre nonzeroness pins the basis coordinate of `q` to a unit, so
    26	  `q` spans `Qₚ`; `PicardGroup`'s `bijective_of_surjective` (invertible target) upgrades
    27	  spanning to bijectivity, and `Module.FinitePresentation.exists_notMem_bijective` spreads
    28	  the stalk bijection to a basic open.
    29	* `Module.exists_notMem_smul_eq_of_tmul_ne_zero` — **the local-rescaling corollary** (the
    30	  N5 engine input): a second element `q'` lies in the `B_f`-span of the local basis `q`,
    31	  so `q' = a • q` in `Q_f` for a scalar `a`.
    32	
    33	Consumers: N5 (the relative uniqueness / mono engine) and the §3.2 chart mono
    34	consume the local basis to rescale the two canonical sections by a unit
    35	(the I-0231-safe route: invertibility of `H⁰`, never "fibrewise ⟹ relative").
    36	-/

    49	/-- **The Nakayama companion — a fibrewise-nonzero element is a Zariski-local basis**
    50	(worksheet GAP-3 companion, deferred from C2/I-0253): for a finite projective `B`-module
    51	`Q` of stalk-rank exactly `1` at the prime `p`, an element `q : Q` whose image in the
    52	fibre `Q ⊗ κ(p)` is nonzero generates `Q` freely on a basic open `D(f) ∋ p`: the map
    53	`x ↦ x • q` is a bijection `B_f → Q_f`.
    54	
    55	Over the local ring `Rₚ` the localized module `Qₚ` is free of rank `1`, so `q`'s basis
    56	coordinate `c` satisfies: if `c` were a non-unit it would lie in the maximal ideal, hence
    57	`q` would vanish in the fibre `κ(p) ⊗ Qₚ ≅ Q ⊗ κ(p)`, contradicting `hq`. Thus `c` is a
    58	unit and `q` spans `Qₚ`; `Module.Invertible`'s `bijective_of_surjective` promotes spanning
    59	to a bijection, and the isomorphism spreads to a basic open. -/
    60	theorem exists_notMem_bijective_toSpanSingleton

    62	    (hrank : Module.rankAtStalk Q p = 1) (q : Q)

    66	  classical
    67	  haveI : Module.FinitePresentation B Q := Module.finitePresentation_of_projective B Q
    68	  set Rₚ := Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal with hRₚ
    69	  set Qₚ := LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q with hQₚ
    70	  set mkq : Qₚ := LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q q with hmkq
    71	  -- `Qₚ` is finite, flat and hence free of rank `1` over the local ring `Rₚ`
    72	  haveI : Module.Free Rₚ Qₚ := Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing
    73	  have hrank1 : Module.finrank Rₚ Qₚ = 1 := hrank
    74	  -- a basis of the free rank-`1` module, and the coordinate of `mkq`
    75	  set b : Module.Basis Unit Rₚ Qₚ := Module.basisUnique Unit hrank1 with hb
    76	  set c : Rₚ := b.repr mkq default with hc
    77	  have hmkq_eq : mkq = c • b default := by
    78	    have hsum := b.sum_repr mkq
    79	    rw [Fintype.sum_unique, ← hc] at hsum

    89	    set ε : κ ⊗[Rₚ] Qₚ →ₗ[Rₚ] κ ⊗[B] Q :=
    90	      (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange B Rₚ κ κ Q).toLinearMap.restrictScalars Rₚ

    92	    have hηmkq : η mkq = (1 : Rₚ) ⊗ₜ[B] q := by
    93	      rw [hη, hmkq, LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap_apply,
    94	        LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct_apply_mk, Localization.mk_one]

    97	        LinearEquiv.lTensor_tmul, hηmkq,
    98	        TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange_tmul, one_smul]
    99	    -- but `1 ⊗ mkq = 0` since `c ∈ maximalIdeal` kills the residue
   100	    have hcres : c • (1 : κ) = 0 := by
   101	      rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_one, IsLocalRing.ResidueField.algebraMap_eq]
   102	      exact (IsLocalRing.residue_eq_zero_iff c).mpr hcmem
   103	    have hzero : (1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[Rₚ] mkq = 0 := by
   104	      rw [hmkq_eq, ← TensorProduct.smul_tmul, hcres, TensorProduct.zero_tmul]

   108	      rw [show (q ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : κ) : Q ⊗[B] κ)

   142	/-- **The local-rescaling corollary** (the N5 engine input): with `q` a local basis at
   143	`p` (rank `1`, fibrewise nonzero), any second element `q'` lies in the `B_f`-span of `q`,

/-!
# Local properties about linear maps

In this file, we show that
injectivity, surjectivity, bijectivity and exactness of linear maps are local properties.
More precisely, we show that these can be checked at maximal ideals and on standard covers.
-/

public section

open Submodule LocalizedModule Ideal LinearMap

section isLocalized_maximal

open IsLocalizedModule

variable {R M N L : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
  [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [AddCommMonoid L] [Module R L]

-- For every maximal ideal `p` of `R`, let `Mₚ` (resp. `Nₚ`, resp. `Lₚ`) the localizations
-- of `M` (resp. `N`, resp. `L`) at `p`.
variable
  (Rₚ : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Type*)
  [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], CommSemiring (Rₚ P)]
  [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Algebra R (Rₚ P)]
  [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], IsLocalization.AtPrime (Rₚ P) P]
  (Mₚ : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Type*)
  [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], AddCommMonoid (Mₚ P)]
  [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Module R (Mₚ P)]
  [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Module (Rₚ P) (Mₚ P)]
  [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], IsScalarTower R (Rₚ P) (Mₚ P)]
  (f : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], M →ₗ[R] Mₚ P)
  [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], IsLocalizedModule.AtPrime P (f P)]
  (Nₚ : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Type*)
  [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], AddCommMonoid (Nₚ P)]
  [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Module R (Nₚ P)]
  (g : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], N →ₗ[R] Nₚ P)
  [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], IsLocalizedModule.AtPrime P (g P)]
  (Lₚ : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Type*)
  [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], AddCommMonoid (Lₚ P)]
  [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Module R (Lₚ P)]
  (h : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], L →ₗ[R] Lₚ P)
  [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], IsLocalizedModule.AtPrime P (h P)]
  (F : M →ₗ[R] N) (G : N →ₗ[R] L)

theorem injective_of_isLocalized_maximal
    (H : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Function.Injective (map P.primeCompl (f P) (g P) F)) :
    Function.Injective F :=
  fun x y eq ↦ Module.eq_of_localization_maximal _ f _ _ fun P _ ↦ H P <| by simp [eq]

theorem surjective_of_isLocalized_maximal
    (H : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Function.Surjective (map P.primeCompl (f P) (g P) F)) :
    Function.Surjective F :=
  range_eq_top.mp <| eq_top_of_localization₀_maximal Nₚ g _ <|
    fun P _ ↦ (range_localizedMap_eq_localized₀_range _ (f P) (g P) F).symm.trans <|
    range_eq_top.mpr <| H P

theorem bijective_of_isLocalized_maximal
    (H : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Function.Bijective (map P.primeCompl (f P) (g P) F)) :
    Function.Bijective F :=
  ⟨injective_of_isLocalized_maximal Mₚ f Nₚ g F fun J _ ↦ (H J).1,
  surjective_of_isLocalized_maximal Mₚ f Nₚ g F fun J _ ↦ (H J).2⟩

theorem exact_of_isLocalized_maximal (H : ∀ (J : Ideal R) [J.IsMaximal],
    Function.Exact (map J.primeCompl (f J) (g J) F) (map J.primeCompl (g J) (h J) G)) :
    Function.Exact F G := by
  simp only [LinearMap.exact_iff] at H ⊢
  apply eq_of_localization₀_maximal Nₚ g
  intro J hJ
  rw [← LinearMap.range_localizedMap_eq_localized₀_range _ (f J) (g J) F,
    ← LinearMap.ker_localizedMap_eq_localized₀_ker J.primeCompl (g J) (h J) G]
  have := SetLike.ext_iff.mp <| H J
  ext x
  simp only [mem_range, mem_ker] at this ⊢
  exact this x

theorem LinearIndependent.of_isLocalized_maximal {ι} (v : ι → M)
    (H : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], LinearIndependent (Rₚ P) (f P ∘ v)) :
    LinearIndependent R v :=
  injective_of_isLocalized_maximal _ (fun P _ ↦ Finsupp.mapRange.linearMap <|
    Algebra.linearMap R (Rₚ P)) _ f _ fun P _ ↦ by rw [map_linearCombination]; exact H P

end isLocalized_maximal

section localized_maximal

variable {R M N L : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
  [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [AddCommMonoid L] [Module R L] (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (g : N →ₗ[R] L)

theorem injective_of_localized_maximal
    (h : ∀ (J : Ideal R) [J.IsMaximal], Function.Injective (map J.primeCompl f)) :
    Function.Injective f :=
  injective_of_isLocalized_maximal _ (fun _ _ ↦ mkLinearMap _ _) _ (fun _ _ ↦ mkLinearMap _ _) f h

theorem surjective_of_localized_maximal
    (h : ∀ (J : Ideal R) [J.IsMaximal], Function.Surjective (map J.primeCompl f)) :
    Function.Surjective f :=
  surjective_of_isLocalized_maximal _ (fun _ _ ↦ mkLinearMap _ _) _ (fun _ _ ↦ mkLinearMap _ _) f h

theorem bijective_of_localized_maximal
    (h : ∀ (J : Ideal R) [J.IsMaximal], Function.Bijective (map J.primeCompl f)) :
    Function.Bijective f :=
  ⟨injective_of_localized_maximal _ fun J _ ↦ (h J).1,
  surjective_of_localized_maximal _ fun J _ ↦ (h J).2⟩

theorem exact_of_localized_maximal
    (h : ∀ (J : Ideal R) [J.IsMaximal], Function.Exact (map J.primeCompl f) (map J.primeCompl g)) :
    Function.Exact f g :=
  exact_of_isLocalized_maximal _ (fun _ _ ↦ mkLinearMap _ _) _ (fun _ _ ↦ mkLinearMap _ _)
    _ (fun _ _ ↦ mkLinearMap _ _) f g h

end localized_maximal

section isLocalized_span

open IsLocalizedModule

variable {R M N L : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
  [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [AddCommMonoid L] [Module R L] (s : Set R) (spn : Ideal.span s = ⊤)
include spn

-- For every element `r ∈ s`, let `Mᵣ` (resp. `Nᵣ`, resp. `Lᵣ`) the localizations
-- of `M` (resp. `N`, resp. `L`) away from `r`.
variable
  (Mₚ : ∀ _ : s, Type*)
  [∀ r : s, AddCommMonoid (Mₚ r)]
  [∀ r : s, Module R (Mₚ r)]
  (f : ∀ r : s, M →ₗ[R] Mₚ r)
  [∀ r : s, IsLocalizedModule.Away r.1 (f r)]
  (Nₚ : ∀ _ : s, Type*)
  [∀ r : s, AddCommMonoid (Nₚ r)]
  [∀ r : s, Module R (Nₚ r)]
  (g : ∀ r : s, N →ₗ[R] Nₚ r)
  [∀ r : s, IsLocalizedModule.Away r.1 (g r)]
  (Lₚ : ∀ _ : s, Type*)
  [∀ r : s, AddCommMonoid (Lₚ r)]
  [∀ r : s, Module R (Lₚ r)]
  (h : ∀ r : s, L →ₗ[R] Lₚ r)
  [∀ r : s, IsLocalizedModule.Away r.1 (h r)]
  (F : M →ₗ[R] N) (G : N →ₗ[R] L)

theorem injective_of_isLocalized_span
    (H : ∀ r : s, Function.Injective (map (.powers r.1) (f r) (g r) F)) :
    Function.Injective F :=
  fun x y eq ↦ Module.eq_of_isLocalized_span _ spn _ f _ _ fun P ↦ H P <| by simp [eq]

theorem surjective_of_isLocalized_span
    (H : ∀ r : s, Function.Surjective (map (.powers r.1) (f r) (g r) F)) :
    Function.Surjective F :=
  range_eq_top.mp <| eq_top_of_isLocalized₀_span s spn Nₚ g fun r ↦
    (range_localizedMap_eq_localized₀_range _ (f r) (g r) F).symm.trans <| range_eq_top.mpr <| H r

theorem bijective_of_isLocalized_span
    (H : ∀ r : s, Function.Bijective (map (.powers r.1) (f r) (g r) F)) :
    Function.Bijective F :=
  ⟨injective_of_isLocalized_span _ spn Mₚ f Nₚ g F fun r ↦ (H r).1,
  surjective_of_isLocalized_span _ spn Mₚ f Nₚ g F fun r ↦ (H r).2⟩

lemma exact_of_isLocalized_span (H : ∀ r : s, Function.Exact
    (map (.powers r.1) (f r) (g r) F) (map (.powers r.1) (g r) (h r) G)) :
    Function.Exact F G := by
  simp only [LinearMap.exact_iff] at H ⊢
  apply Submodule.eq_of_isLocalized₀_span s spn Nₚ g
  intro r
  rw [← LinearMap.range_localizedMap_eq_localized₀_range _ (f r) (g r) F]
  rw [← LinearMap.ker_localizedMap_eq_localized₀_ker (.powers r.1) (g r) (h r) G]
  have := SetLike.ext_iff.mp <| H r
  ext x
  simp only [mem_range, mem_ker] at this ⊢
  exact this x

end isLocalized_span

section localized_span

variable {R M N L : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
  [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [AddCommMonoid L] [Module R L]
